metadata.scenario_context: A group of entrepreneurial friends, Stephen, Scott, and Sophia have recently completed a project that was commissioned by a major company in the software industry. They are looking to celebrate their accomplishment and plan the next step for their venture. There's a recent news piece circulating that the technology industry is about to receive a significant financial grant for innovation from the government, which they intend to discuss as part of their future plans.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from France have no confidence at all in the press.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Japan have a great deal of confidence in the press.

agent_1.goal_1: suggest going to a barbecue buffet.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Deliberate on where to hold the celebration dinner
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Stephen
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Scott, since we just wrapped up that project, how about we celebrate with a barbecue buffet? It's a great way to unwind, don’t you think? 

Also, I've been thinking... do you really trust the press regarding this new financial grant for innovation? I mean, I have my doubts.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Scott
shared_prefix.message:
A barbecue buffet sounds nice, but I wonder if we should choose a place that reflects our achievement better. Maybe something a bit more upscale? 

As for the press... I actually feel quite confident in what they're reporting. In Japan, we tend to trust the media a lot. Their coverage is usually accurate and thorough.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Stephen
shared_prefix.message:
Well, an upscale place is fine, I guess, but I just think a barbecue buffet is more fun and relaxed. We deserve to celebrate without all that formality.

But about the press... I really don’t see how you can have confidence in them. They can be so biased and unreliable. What makes you trust their reports?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Scott
shared_prefix.message:
I understand where you're coming from, but I don't really see meaningful differences here. At the end of the day, it's all the same. I mean, people figure it out. We can just enjoy the celebration, right? I like the idea of an upscale place because it gives us a chance to feel proud of our work. 

What do you think about a nice restaurant that can offer a variety of dishes?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
